claims.text: Titanium alloys containing solid-lubricant additives can serve as high-performance, wide-temperature self-lubricating materials.
The proposed material is a titanium alloy containing solid-lubricant additives.
Solid-lubricant additives are added to the titanium alloy.
The material is intended to operate across a wide temperature range under high-temperature conditions.
The solid-lubricant additives form a lubricating film on the material surface.
The surface lubricating film reduces friction.
The surface lubricating film reduces wear.
The titanium-alloy matrix provides mechanical strength.
Adding solid-lubricant additives improves tribological performance across a wide temperature range.
The proposed material provides improved mechanical strength across a wide temperature range.
Traditional self-lubricating materials have a limited operating-temperature range.
The proposed operating-temperature range is -200 °C to 500 °C.
The exact additive composition and proportion needed for optimal performance are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The conditions characterize the entire operating regime as high-temperature, whereas the stated range begins at -200 °C, which is cryogenic rather than high-temperature.

The design specifies a titanium-alloy control without additives, but the falsification rule instead compares the candidate against traditional self-lubricating materials, leaving the decisive comparator inconsistent.
